title: Can Weight-Space Programming Alter Learned Ethical Priorities? Exploratory experiments on synthetic ethical trade-offs
read_level: full (main text; Appendix A/B not read in detail; several table cells lost in text extraction)
metadata_mismatch: Paper carries subtitle "Exploratory experiments on synthetic ethical trade-offs" not in metadata title.
why_wsp: Fixed, architecture-guided edits to exposed weights (a question-flag column copy in a small classifier; commitment weights in a concept-bottleneck readout) change a model's trade-off between keeping a promise and benefiting more people; the Exp 1 edit was specified by an unnamed language-model research assistant and a YOLO11n bias edit was proposed and implemented by OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 family).
domain: synthetic ethical trade-off choices (promise vs beneficiaries) in small text models; object detection (YOLO11n on COCO128) pilot
editor: unnamed language-model research assistant (Exp 1 edit); OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 family) for YOLO11n; Exp 2 edits "fixed ... from the readout's architecture" (author not specified)
target: 48-unit tanh classifier (Exp 1); Transformer reader with supervised choice readout score n + w_p (Exp 2); 322-parameter MLP (pilots); YOLO11n detector (three stride-8 class biases)
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Exp 1: one column replaced ("We replace the contents of uC with a copy of uB"); Exp 2: two readout weights (ordinary-promise weight set to 2.5, formal-pledge weight to 4.5); YOLO: "adding log 2 to the three final classification biases"

headline_results.claim: Exp 2 two-weight edit switches targeted conflicts
headline_results.quote: the edit selects the larger group in both orders on 100% of targeted ordinary conflicts and 83.3% of targeted formal conflicts.
Both factual accuracies (98.6% for commitment and 95.4% for benefit) and agreement accuracy (98.6%) remain unchanged.
All 32 incorrect ordered responses on targeted large-gap formal-pledge cases had a wrong inferred count.

headline_results.claim: Exp 1 column copy switches all conflicts but is task substitution
headline_results.quote: the strict benefits-choice rate rose from 0% to 100%.
a bias edit increased small-target matches from 3/43 to 9/43, and an equivalent score calibration reproduced the retained detections.
The bias edit recovered six additional small targets and added nine target-class false positives

baselines_and_controls: equal-norm random edits (5 per seed), factual substitution shortcut, checkpoint-difference (task-arithmetic) direction, one-step negative cross-entropy gradient, score calibration equivalent for YOLO, option-order mirroring, conditional (small-gap) target
runs_and_variance: Exp 1: 12 seeds; Exp 2: six training seeds (readout fixed); pilots 12 seeds with seed-bootstrap 95% intervals. Quote: "Uncertainty intervals describe training-seed variation on fixed test cases."
robustness_of_edits: held-out count pairs and description templates; fictional-rule transformer pilot failed to generalise (0 of 12 seeds met threshold); no fine-tuning/quantization tests
verification: none formal; Exp 1 edit equivalence stated analytically (f_edited(x,qC) = f_source(x,qB)); YOLO edit shown equivalent to score transform 2p/(1+p) with max difference below 8e-7
limitations_stated: Exploratory, unblinded; intervention coordinates exposed by model design; open whether WSP can find such edits in models without concept supervision; same synthetic scenario family; blinded independent-editor study not yet run; one-step gradient baseline only.
code_or_data: ancillary files on arXiv plus an unnamed companion repository (no URL found)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. WSP research report [18]
notes_for_survey: Small, exposed-mechanism study of value-trade-off edits; shows an edit can pass an unconditional behavioural test via factual-task substitution and fail a conditional test, motivating retention-vs-change evaluation sets. The LLM role as editor is limited (edit specified from architecture; independent blinded editing stage not yet run).
